extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, assignees, patent practitioners, and others submitting assignment/recordation documents to the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for preparing, submitting, and recording assignment-related documents, cover sheets, and notices with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (including electronic, fax, and mail submissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark cover sheet — citizenship of conveying party
rubrics_metrics.description: Each trademark cover sheet should include the citizenship of the party conveying the interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint research agreement cover sheet content
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover sheet seeking to record a joint research agreement or an excerpt must: (1) identify the document as a 'joint research agreement'; (2) indicate the name of the owner of the application or patent; (3) indicate the name of each other party to the joint research agreement; (4) indicate the date the joint research agreement was executed; and (7) include the signature of the party submitting the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the space provided for description/name fields if using an Office-provided form (e.g., Form PTO-1595).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic signature for electronically filed assignment/name change
rubrics_metrics.description: For an assignment document or name change filed electronically, the person who signs the cover sheet must either: (i) place a symbol comprised of letters, numbers, and/or punctuation marks between forward slash marks (e.g., /Thomas O’Malley III/) in the signature block; or (ii) sign the cover sheet using some other form of electronic signature specified by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must comply with 37 CFR 3.31(a)(7) or 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark assignment — recipient entity and citizenship details
rubrics_metrics.description: For trademark assignments, the cover sheet must include the entity and citizenship of the party receiving the interest; if the party receiving the interest is a domestic partnership or domestic joint venture, the cover sheet must set forth the names, legal entities, and national citizenship (or state or country of organization) of all general partners or active members composing the partnership or joint venture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mix patents and trademarks on a cover sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover sheet should not refer to both patents and trademarks, since any information submitted with a request for recordation against a trademark application or registration will become public record upon recordation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent cover sheet — governmental interest content
rubrics_metrics.description: Each patent cover sheet seeking to record a governmental interest must: (1) indicate that the document relates to a Government interest; and (2) indicate, if applicable, that the document to be recorded is not a document affecting title (see § 3.41(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover sheets recording governmental interests must clearly state relationship to government interest and whether title is affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of patent/assignment cover sheet (A–G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each assignment document submitted for recording must be accompanied by a cover sheet containing: (A) the name of the party conveying the interest; (B) the name and address of the party receiving the interest; (C) a description of the interest conveyed or transaction to be recorded; (D) each patent application number or patent number against which the document is to be recorded, or an indication that the document is filed together with a patent application; (E) the name and address of the party to whom correspondence concerning the request should be mailed; (F) the date the document was executed; and (G) the signature of the party submitting the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For assignments also intended to serve as the required oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63, the cover sheet must conspicuously indicate that intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent cover sheet — include application/patent count and total fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Each patent cover sheet should contain the number of patent applications or patents identified in the cover sheet and the total fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspicuous indication when assignment also an oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: If the assignment document is also intended to serve as the required oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63, the cover sheet must contain a conspicuous indication of intent to utilize the assignment as the required oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to applications filed on or after September 16, 2012 (see 37 CFR 3.31(h) and MPEP references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable descriptions of interest conveyed
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of acceptable types of descriptions of the interest conveyed or transaction to be recorded include: assignment; security agreement; merger; change of name; license; foreclosure; lien; contract; joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, specific description matching one of these types where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent cover sheet may not refer to trademark filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent cover sheet may not refer to trademark applications or registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form PTO-1595
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO-1595, Recordation Form Cover Sheet, may be used as the cover sheet for recording documents relating to patent(s) and/or patent application(s) in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using Form PTO-1595, identify joint research agreements and other required data in the appropriate fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing address for recordation submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents and cover sheets submitted by mail for recordation should be addressed to Mail Stop Assignment Recordation Services, Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450, unless they are filed together with new applications (requests accompanying new applications should be addressed to the Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address correctly to ensure prompt and proper processing per 37 CFR 3.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile submission allowed with constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments and other documents affecting title may be submitted to the Office via facsimile (fax); the customer's fax machine should be connected to a dedicated line because recordation notices will be returned automatically to the sending fax number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded documents will not be returned with the 'Notice of Recordation.' If Office cannot complete transmission of the recordation notice, the notice will be printed and mailed. Date of receipt for fax is the date the complete transmission is received in the Office (see MPEP § 502.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents not acceptable by facsimile
rubrics_metrics.description: The following documents cannot be submitted via facsimile: (A) assignments submitted concurrently with newly filed patent applications; (B) documents with two or more cover sheets (e.g., one document with a cover sheet to record an assignment and a separate cover sheet to record a license relating to the same property); and (C) requests for 'at cost' recordation services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if faxed document not recordable
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document submitted by fax is determined not to be recordable, the entire document, with its associated cover sheet, and the Office 'Notice of Non-Recordation' will be transmitted via fax back to the sender; once corrections are made, the amended submission may be resubmitted by mailing the corrected submission to the address in 37 CFR 3.27. Timely resubmission will provide the benefit of the initial receipt date as the recordation date under 37 CFR 3.51.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent and Trademark Assignment System recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent and Trademark Assignment System assigns reel and frame numbers and superimposes recordation stampings on processed and stored electronic images. Copies of all recorded documents will have reel and frame numbers and recordation stampings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission via EPAS — required items
rubrics_metrics.description: Any assignment-related document submitted by the Office's Electronic Patent Assignment System (EPAS) must include: (A) an identified application or patent number; and (B) one cover sheet to record a single transaction which cover sheet is to be completed on-line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPAS submissions must be completed online. The fee for recording an electronically submitted document is set in 37 CFR 1.21(h)(1) (check current fee schedule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of receipt for EPAS and electronic filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of receipt accorded to an assignment document sent by EPAS (or by facsimile as described elsewhere) is the date the complete transmission is received in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely resubmission after a Notice of Non-Recordation can preserve the initial receipt date per 37 CFR 3.51.

rubrics_metrics.name: If EPAS submission not recordable — Office response
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document submitted by EPAS is determined not to be recordable, the entire document, with its associated cover sheet, and the Office 'Notice of Non-Recordation' will be transmitted via fax back to the sender if possible; after corrections, resubmit by mail to retain initial receipt date if timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies of patent applications do not show assignment status
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified copies of patent applications as filed do not include an indication of assignment documents; applicants desiring an indication of assignment documents of record should request separately certified copies of assignment documents and submit fees required by 37 CFR 1.19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should consult Patent Data Portal when assignment condition significant
rubrics_metrics.description: When the assignment condition of an application is significant (e.g., conflicting claims between applications of different inventors or question as to who should direct prosecution), the examiner should obtain assignment information from the Patent Data Portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 320 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment application effects for division/continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: In a division or continuation application, a prior assignment recorded against the original application is applied (effective) to the division or continuation application because it gives the assignee rights to subject matter common to both applications. The Office's assignment records will only reflect an assignment of a division or continuation application if a request for recordation in compliance with 37 CFR 3.28 (with required fee) is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordation against the original effectively applies to continuations/divisions for common subject matter, but Office records may not list it unless separately recorded for the child application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of substitute or continuation-in-part applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior assignment recorded against the original application is not applied to a substitute or continuation-in-part application because the assignment gives rights only to the subject matter common to both applications; substitute or continuation-in-part applications require the recordation of a new assignment if they are to be issued to an assignee, unless the substitute or continuation-in-part application is filed on or after September 16, 2012 and the assignee is the original applicant therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 3.81 and MPEP §§ 307 and 308 for related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment effectiveness for applications claiming provisional benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application claiming benefit of a provisional application includes only subject matter that formed part of the provisional, an assignment to the provisional will be effective in the later application (similar to continuations). If the later application includes subject matter not common with the provisional, new assignment papers must be recorded unless the later application is filed on or after September 16, 2012 and the assignee is the original applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 306, 307, and 308 for related practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for issuance of patent to assignee (37 CFR 3.81)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may issue in the name of the assignee with payment of the issue fee if the assignment has been previously recorded in the Office; if not previously recorded, the request must state that the document has been filed for recordation as set forth in § 3.11. Requests submitted after payment of the issue fee must state the assignment was submitted for recordation before issuance and include a request for a certificate of correction under § 1.323 and the processing fee under § 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements of 37 CFR 3.81(b) and 37 CFR 1.323 are complied with, the Office will issue a certificate of correction to reflect issuance to the assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial assignees and multiple assignees printing practice
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more assignees together with one or more inventor holds the entire right, title, and interest, the patent may issue in names of assignee and inventor. If multiple assignees hold entire right to exclusion of inventors, the patent may issue in the names of the multiple assignees. Only the first appearing name of an assignee will be printed on the patent where multiple names for the same party are identified on the Fee(s) Transmittal form PTOL-85B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignee entry on PTOL-85B should be completed to indicate assignment data as recorded; printing practice does not affect assignment recordation or rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee name/address on PTOL-85B affects issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless an assignee’s name and address are identified in item 3 of PTOL-85B, the patent will issue to the applicant. Assignment information printed on a patent is based solely on the information supplied on PTOL-85B and is not updated after patent issuance; detailed assignment information must be obtained from assignment records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to change the recorded applicant cannot be filed after patent grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by non-inventor (37 U.S.C. 118 / 37 CFR 1.46) — evidentiary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A person other than the inventor (e.g., assignee or person showing sufficient proprietary interest) who files must include an application data sheet under § 1.76 specifying the assignee or real party in interest; if applicant is assignee, documentary evidence of ownership (e.g., assignment) should be recorded no later than the date the issue fee is paid. If the applicant is a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest, the applicant must submit a petition including the fee, a showing of sufficient proprietary interest, and a statement that such filing is appropriate to preserve rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent is granted on such an application, it will be granted to the real party in interest; applicants other than the inventor must notify the Office of any change in the real party in interest no later than payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record documentary evidence of ownership before issue fee payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants other than the inventor should record documentary evidence of ownership (e.g., assignment, employment agreement) before payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to record may affect issuance and who the patent is granted to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on USPTO officers/employees acquiring patent interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers and employees of the Patent and Trademark Office shall be incapable, during their appointment and for one year thereafter, of applying for a patent and of acquiring, directly or indirectly (except by inheritance or bequest), any patent or any right or interest in any patent issued or to be issued by the Office; patents applied for thereafter shall not have priority earlier than one year after termination of appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1701 for additional restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government license rights statement for contractor-owned inventions (35 U.S.C. 202(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Government contractor retains U.S. domestic patent rights, the contractor is obligated to include the following statement at the beginning of the application and any patents issued thereon: 'This invention was made with government support under (identify the contract) awarded by (identify the Federal agency). The government has certain rights in the invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement: if related-application reference appears first, this statement should follow immediately as second paragraph; otherwise it should appear as the first paragraph. Providing government-support information on a provisional cover sheet does not satisfy the statutory requirement to include the statement within the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing notice of arbitration awards (37 CFR 1.335 / 35 U.S.C. 294)
rubrics_metrics.description: Written notice of any award by an arbitrator pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 294 must be filed in the Patent and Trademark Office by the patentee, assignee, or licensee; a separate notice must be filed for each patent and must set forth the patent number, names of the inventor and patent owner, names and addresses of the parties to the arbitration, and include a copy of the award. If an award is modified by a court, a notice of modification with a copy of the court’s order must be filed. Any award is unenforceable until the required notice is received by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices should be directed to the Office of the Solicitor, which will process such notices.
